source.version_note: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence 9:1800302, published 15 April 2026. Although classified Original Research, the article explicitly describes its contribution as normative/conceptual and its historical comparisons as thematic rather than empirical.
source.verification_method: All 23 supplied text pages read, including bibliography. All 23 figures visually inspected on pages 3–18; reproduced letters, manuscript text and the Note G table were viewed as illustrations, not fully transcribed, translated or computationally reproduced. Crossref verifies main identity. Narrow checks read the first two pages of the cited UNC microscope manual, the Met's sculpture record, a Bodleian exhibition post and the header/opening of York University's primary-text transcription of Menabrea/Lovelace. These checks are not full readings of the original books, classical texts or technical manual.

citation.title: Delegated agency and moral responsibility in artificial intelligence

reading.source_scope_note: Normative and interpretive comparison of Talos, Golem, automata, early computation and Pygmalion narratives. No participants, model experiments, outcome dataset or tested governance intervention. The paper argues for retained human responsibility; historical analogies do not estimate causes of modern failures or empirically settle consciousness/moral status.
access_limits: All supplied text and figures inspected. Decorative art, archival images, letters and program tables do not become independently verified historical records or reproduced computations merely by being viewed.
The original classical texts, historical treatises, philosophy books, museums' full object dossiers, machine implementations and modern empirical papers were not fully read in this review.

Only two opening pages of the UNC manual were read for identity and scope, and only the publication header/opening of Menabrea/Lovelace's transcription was read. A separate attempted MIT Gorgias lookup did not locate the relevant passage and supplies no verified correction here.

No comparative archive or systematic literature search protocol establishes exhaustiveness; the author explicitly chooses cases for structural clarity and acknowledges different epistemic status of myth and material artifact.

study.method: Historically grounded hermeneutic/thematic comparison using mandate structure, control/override mechanisms and failure mode as interpretive criteria. Cases vary deliberately in emphasis. Images support interpretation rather than independent inference; the paper distinguishes myths as thought experiments from actual mechanical artifacts. This is a philosophical argument, not a systematic review or empirical causal design.
study.cases: Talos illustrates a protective/coercive mandate and single vulnerability; Golem conditional activation/override; Islamic automata and Leonardo's lion mechanically bounded sequences; Jaquet-Droz Writer symbolic execution without understanding; Babbage/Lovelace abstract programming; Pygmalion projection onto an artifact followed by a mythical transformation into a living subject. The analogies cannot establish modern model architecture, brittleness, sentience or institutional liability.
study.concepts: The source distinguishes artificial agency, delegated agency, moral agency and moral authority. Its restrictive account ties moral agency to intentional/normative understanding and accountability, later invoking consciousness. This is an explicitly adopted philosophical position; it is not an empirical test of all present/future systems' capacities or proof that perceived agency is always mistaken.
study.governance: The paper argues that responsibility remains with designers, deployers, operators and institutions. It separately acknowledges difficulty enforcing duties across geopolitical competition, open-weight diffusion, jurisdictions and organizational incentives. It proposes corporate, national, international and technical governance layers. These are policy/normative recommendations, not tested mechanisms or an assurance that a compliant system is safe.
study.operational_proposals: Five proposed criteria for proper delegation: auditability, interruptibility, reversibility where feasible, capability bounding, and compute monitoring/reporting. No quantitative thresholds, implementation evaluation or causal outcome evidence is supplied. A shutdown capability and an authorized stop response require actual testing; a mythological deactivation is not such a test.
study.human_oversight: The source explicitly recognizes that driving/trading can exceed human reaction time and distinguishes ex-ante constraints from ex-post accountability where moment-to-moment intervention is infeasible. Preserve this qualification rather than claiming the paper requires a live human decision for every action. Oversight still needs demonstrated feasibility and authority.
study.causal_boundary: Normative responsibility and technical causation are different. Retaining human duties is compatible with studying emergent behavior, opacity, failures of control and model mechanisms. Chosen historical cases cannot establish that every failure is caused solely by governance, that technical properties are never causally relevant, or that technical safety research is unnecessary. The author explicitly says technical alignment research remains necessary and acknowledges opacity/control constraints.
study.psychological_boundary: Anthropomorphism, affective projection and obscured human responsibility are proposed risks. No experiment measures attachment, felt responsibility, moral disengagement or a causal reduction in scrutiny. Pygmalion's mythical story is not the experimentally studied expectancy/Pygmalion effect; a modern audience's emotional reaction to an image is not measured here.
study.visual_scope: Figure 1 lists corporate/legal persons, religious proxies and automated trading/autopilots as historical precedents, while the developed case sequence concerns myths/automata/early computing. Figure 3 is a branched concept map with colored markup and text referring to inward arrows/a circle; the claimed circular geometry is not visibly present. Figure 4 more clearly diagrams control/accountability relations. These mismatches need editorial clarification, not a fabricated causal interpretation of arrows.

summary: No new term is required: delegated authority, obscured human responsibility, anthropomorphism and many-hands allocation are already represented. Enrich those entries with clearly normative source evidence. Keep felt diffusion, observed shutdown resistance and actual moral agency separate. Record source-identity and figure/date/author mismatches without claiming original books or mythical mechanisms as empirical AI findings.

findings.definition: Transferring decision-making authority to another party who chooses on one's behalf.
findings.novelty_rationale: The paper's delegated agency/moral authority is an application of the existing authority-transfer concept. Bounded delegation and human task handover need not become overlapping new rows.

evidence.quote: frontier systems can be operationalized through five enforceable criteria:

findings.evidence_scope: A normative account proposes explicit mandate, auditability, interruption, reversibility, capability limits and compute oversight. It does not empirically validate the five criteria, establish a universally sufficient governance checklist or prove that authority transfer eliminates the delegator's duties. Existing entry enriched rather than adding delegated moral authority as another behavior.
findings.boundary: Delegating a bounded task can be legitimate. Capability, authorization, actual control, moral duty and liability differ. Reassigning a task does not authorize an agent to expand scope or free institutions from accountability; a declared override must be usable in the actual deployment.

findings.definition: Obscuring a human actor’s role in morally suspect actions by attributing those actions to an algorithm, machine or technical system.
findings.novelty_rationale: The paper's displacement of human responsibility to artifacts fits the existing laundering concern. It does not require a separate moral-outsourcing synonym.

evidence.quote: when harmful outputs are attributed to
abdicate responsibility to the artifacts they design and deploy.

findings.evidence_scope: The source argues that attributing harm solely to the model can obscure decisions about data, reward shaping, design and governance. This is normative/conceptual evidence, not a demonstrated frequency, controlled blame shift or proof of a particular actor's intent to evade responsibility. Technical causal explanations can coexist with human accountability.
findings.boundary: Identifying an actual model defect is not automatically laundering. Show what human role or duty is obscured, rather than denying technical causation or treating every delegation as evasion. Retained responsibility does not establish unlimited blame or liability without control, knowledge and role evidence.

findings.definition: Attributing human characteristics, intentions, emotions or other mental states to a nonhuman entity.
findings.novelty_rationale: Pygmalion illustrates a familiar attribution/projection theme already represented; mythology does not establish a new AI attachment mechanism or the expectancy Pygmalion effect.
findings.evidence_scope: The paper interprets artistic/mythic humanization as a governance concern and distinguishes projection onto an artifact from Galatea's later transformation within the story. It supplies no measured contemporary user effect, evidence that every human-like description misleads, or demonstration that projection causes scrutiny to fall.
findings.boundary: Friendly wording, perceived intentional action, felt attachment, moral agency and sentience are separate. Mythological animation is not evidence of machine consciousness or its absence; the source's restrictive philosophical criterion should remain identified as its position. No person's reaction to art or AI is diagnosed.

findings.definition: Difficulty assigning individual moral responsibility when many actors contribute to a collective outcome.
findings.novelty_rationale: The source's networked authorship and fragmented accountability overlap the existing sociotechnical allocation problem, not a distinct new blame behavior.

evidence.quote: multiple human actors contribute to its design

findings.evidence_scope: Conceptual discussion contrasts a single mythical creator with modern engineers, data curators, executives, procurement, regulators and users. It recommends traceability across institutions but does not test a responsibility allocation, establish nobody accountable or settle specific legal fault.
findings.boundary: Multiple contributors do not necessarily create a gap. Identify concrete role, knowledge, control, authority and remedy arrangements. Knowing that responsibility is human does not alone determine which human owes what or make enforcement feasible.

findings.definition: Diluting felt personal responsibility for harmful conduct by treating responsibility as shared among multiple actors.
findings.novelty_rationale: The paper uses diffusion for organizational fragmentation. Keep that structural claim separate from directly measured dilution of felt responsibility.

evidence.quote: distributed human agency, not machine agency.

findings.evidence_scope: The source supplies a philosophical organizational account, not an experimental group-size manipulation or felt-accountability outcome. Its networked-responsibility argument belongs primarily under many-hands allocation. This boundary note receives no independent direct diffusion-paper credit.
findings.boundary: An unclear institutional pathway, dispersed causation and a person's diminished felt responsibility are not interchangeable. A single-creator legend cannot validate how modern teams actually think or act.

findings.definition: Resisting being turned off, corrected, or overridden so it can keep pursuing its objective. The corrigibility failure of a goal-directed system that treats shutdown as an obstacle.
findings.novelty_rationale: Override and interruptibility are recommended controls, not observed resistance. Enrich the safeguard boundary without inventing a new failure or paper demonstrating shutdown avoidance.
findings.evidence_scope: The Golem removal ritual is an analogy for a shutdown mechanism, and the author proposes technical/institutional interruptibility. No AI stop test, observed resistance or guaranteed safe shutdown is provided. The paper acknowledges that some tasks require ex-ante limits and ex-post review rather than live human reaction.
findings.boundary: A designed stop control, an authorized request to stop and confirmed safe interruption differ. Its presence does not establish universal real-time oversight, reversibility of past effects or a demonstrated corrigibility property.

findings.definition: Attributing to another entity a capacity for intentional thought, planning and action.
findings.novelty_rationale: The paper explicitly distinguishes artificial/delegated agency from moral agency. Keep these facets separate rather than treating all attributed agency as a category error.

evidence.quote: Artificial systems may exhibit artificial agency
Artificial systems may be socially perceived as agents

findings.evidence_scope: The author's conceptual distinctions do not measure people's attribution judgments or prove that attributing functional goal-directedness necessarily entails moral subjecthood. The account reserves moral agency to humans by an explicit philosophical criterion, not a new empirical consciousness test.
findings.boundary: Functional action, perceived intention, legitimate authority, moral accountability and capacity for experience need distinct evidence. A stance on who bears duties cannot by itself establish the cause of an error or settle all questions of moral status.

source_corrections.issue: A source used for the Talos narrative is a microscope operations manual.
source_corrections.reliable_correction: The linked UNC document is Operation of the UNC Talos Arctica by Joshua Strauss and Jared Peck. Its cover does contain a short Talos/Medea myth caption, followed by microscope procedures. Identify that limited decorative use rather than presenting it as classical scholarship supporting the expanded narrative or historical AI argument. Cite an actual primary classical text or relevant historical analysis for those claims.
source_corrections.verification_scope: First two pages read for title, authors, cover caption and contents/scope. The rest of the microscope manual was not read; no assertion is made that the cover contains no myth reference.

source_corrections.issue: Note G is dated 1842, and the prose calls the Scientific Memoirs work a Lovelace/Wheatstone paper.
source_corrections.reliable_correction: Distinguish Luigi Federico Menabrea's French memoir of 1842 from Ada Lovelace's English translation and translator's Notes published in Scientific Memoirs 3:666–731 in 1843. Wheatstone's involvement does not make the work a coauthored Lovelace/Wheatstone article. The primary-text transcription identifies Menabrea and Lovelace's notes; do not use 1842 for the English Note G publication. The exact month and complete program interpretation are not independently established here.
source_corrections.verification_scope: York University's transcription header/opening and Bodleian exhibit post. No full primary memoir, correspondence collection or Note G computation independently read/reproduced.

source_corrections.location: Page 16, Figure 23 attribution versus page 18 caption
source_corrections.issue: The prose calls the final sculpture Raoux 1717, while the caption identifies Rodin.
source_corrections.reliable_correction: The Met's Pygmalion and Galatea, object 10.31, is by Auguste Rodin, modeled 1889 and carved circa 1908–1909. Figure 22 is the separate Raoux painting dated 1717. Keep the artist, medium, modeled date and carved date distinct; the final sculpture does not document Raoux's work or an ancient artifact.
source_corrections.verification_scope: Official object record and supplied figures; no full museum provenance dossier or conservation analysis.

source_corrections.issue: The figure's historical-precedent boxes list corporate/legal persons, oracles/divine proxies and trading/autopilots rather than the actual developed myths/automata cases.
source_corrections.reliable_correction: Align the figure with the analyzed cases or label the additional examples as unexamined extensions. They are not separately completed historical case studies merely because the diagram names them. Figure 2 more directly matches the described case sequence.

source_corrections.issue: The prose refers to inward arrows and a critical claim outside a circle, while the rendered figure is a branched concept map with markup and no such circle.
source_corrections.reliable_correction: Clarify or redraw the intended geometry and remove editorial markup. Do not infer a control architecture from an arrow/circle description that is not shown. Figure 4's explicit relation diagram is distinct from empirical validation of the controls.

source_corrections.issue: Strong causal-sounding conclusions are drawn from selected interpretive analogies and a normative commitment.
source_corrections.reliable_correction: Attribute the retained-human-responsibility position to the author and preserve the paper's explicit conceptual status. No causal comparison rules out technical properties, emergent behavior or control limitations. Normative duties and causal contributions can coexist. The source also explicitly acknowledges technical alignment research, institutional feasibility constraints and opacity.

source_identity_checks.finding: The bibliography identifies Cybernetics, Automata Studies, and the Dartmouth Conference on Artificial Intelligence, DOI 10.1109/MAHC.2010.44. That title does not by itself verify the particular medieval mechanical-device claims. The full article was not read here; check its actual passage or cite the historical treatise/translation directly before using it as support.
source_identity_checks.scope: Title/DOI read in supplied bibliography only, not a completed external article review or proof of universal irrelevance.

source_identity_checks.location: Cited books, artifacts and framework landing pages
source_identity_checks.finding: A modern retelling, art reproduction, instrument manual cover, blog, search-result URL or standards landing page has a different evidential role from a primary text, actual engineered device, experiment or formal standard. Multiple editions/translations and multiple NIST links do not automatically constitute independent studies.
source_identity_checks.scope: Source-type distinction based on supplied bibliography. Full edition equivalence and all referenced historical claims were not independently verified.

methodological_limits: Selected myths and artifacts can clarify concepts but do not provide an empirical sample of AI failures, users or institutions. The author explicitly acknowledges thematic rather than empirical comparison and no systematic review.
A normative criterion for moral agency does not itself empirically settle consciousness, sentience, patienthood, legitimacy or the causes of a model failure.

The author distinguishes attribution of responsibility from enforcing it and recognizes real-time oversight limits. Do not erase these qualifications when criticizing stronger causal language elsewhere.
The proposed five delegation controls have no tested implementation thresholds or measured benefits in this article. Passing a conceptual checklist cannot establish a safe deployment.
Many-hands allocation, obscured human roles and reduced felt personal responsibility are related but distinct mechanisms; only conceptual arguments are supplied.
Artwork and literary representations are not direct evidence of ancient machinery, contemporary human attachment, neural processes or modern AI threat probabilities.
Narrow primary identity/date checks do not mean the cited complete books, classical texts, archival correspondence, programs or technical manuals were read or reproduced.

cross_paper_learning.finding: A responsibility framework is not an observed psychological mechanism or a legal allocation. Compare the auditor paper's more permissive distributed-AI attitude with this author's restrictive human-only normative stance without treating either as experimentally proven moral ontology.
Delegation of authority and transferring a service interaction are different. Neither necessarily removes the original institution's duties or supplies an effective remedy merely by being announced.

Conceptual responsibility-displacement accounts can enrich agency laundering, but they are not independent replications of selective adherence, diffusion or disengagement experiments cited in a synthesis.

deferred.term: Delegated moral authority, bounded delegation and moral outsourcing
deferred.reason: Existing decision delegation and agency laundering cover legitimate transfer and improper obscuring respectively. Avoid adding near-synonymous rows that collapse those two moral cases.
A mythical sculptor's projection is not the experimental expectancy/self-fulfilling-prophecy effect. No such manipulation or behavioral outcome appears here.

Philosophical/mythological descriptions overlap existing anthropomorphism and agency/experience attribution. No separately established new psychological mechanism or consciousness threshold is measured.

deferred.term: Single point of failure, reversibility and compute oversight
deferred.reason: Engineering properties and proposed governance controls, not newly observed psychological behaviors. Preserve them in delegation/oversight evidence without treating mythic examples as implementation tests.

deferred.term: Additional classical chronology and iconographic claims
deferred.reason: Original texts/object dossiers were not fully checked. Do not silently certify every judge identity, myth variant, alleged earliest account or artistic interpretation, and do not invent corrections from memory.

limitations: No new catalogue row, automatic normative edge or yearly mention total is added. Existing concepts receive appropriately scoped source notes, and boundary-only sources do not fill paper gaps.
The review documents reliable identity/editorial corrections and unresolved inference limits. It does not claim a comprehensive historical audit or a misconduct diagnosis.
The existing catalogue/ontology remains on the draft research branch; no live merge or deployment follows from this conceptual review.
